title: The Scientific Method
passage:
Maya was a natural problem-solver. When she noticed that the prize-winning lilies in her grandmother’s garden were wilting while the daisies right next to them were thriving, she didn't just shrug her shoulders. She decided to use the **scientific method** to uncover the cause.

First, Maya made an **observation**: the lilies looked limp and yellow, but only the ones on the left side of the garden bed. This led her to ask a specific question: 'Why are the lilies on the left side wilting while the ones on the right are healthy?'

Before starting any tests, Maya needed a **hypothesis**. She remembered seeing a small patch of fuzzy white fungus on the soil near the sick plants. She formed an educated guess: 'If the soil on the left side contains a harmful fungus, then the lilies planted there will wilt.'

To test this, she designed a controlled experiment. She took six identical lily bulbs and planted them in six separate pots with the same type of soil. In three of the pots (the experimental group), she added a sample of the white fungus she found in the garden. In the other three pots (the control group), she added nothing but water. She ensured every pot received the exact same amount of sunlight and water each day so that the fungus was the only **variable** being tested.

Over the next two weeks, Maya was **meticulous** about recording her data. She measured the height of the stalks and noted the color of the leaves in her science journal every morning. By the end of the second week, the results were **conclusive**. The lilies in the pots with the fungus were yellow and drooping, just like the ones in the garden. The lilies in the control group were tall, green, and vibrant.

Maya began to **analyze** her findings. The data clearly supported her original hypothesis. She concluded that the fungus was indeed the culprit. She shared her results with her grandmother, and together they treated the garden soil to remove the fungus. Within a month, the garden was once again **abundant** with beautiful, healthy lilies. Maya felt a sense of pride; she hadn't just guessed at a solution—she had proven it.

questions.question: What was the first step Maya took in her scientific journey?
choices: She planted six identical lily bulbs
She made an observation about the wilting lilies
She treated the soil with medicine
She wrote a report for her grandmother
questions.answer: She made an observation about the wilting lilies

questions.question: In Maya's experiment, what was the 'variable'?
choices: The amount of sunlight the pots received
The type of pots used for planting
The presence of the white fungus in the soil
The amount of water given to each plant
questions.answer: The presence of the white fungus in the soil

questions.question: Why did Maya include a 'control group' of three pots with no fungus?
choices: To see if lilies could grow without any soil at all
To make sure she had enough flowers for a bouquet
To compare them against the pots with fungus to see if the fungus was actually causing the change
To save money on fungus samples
questions.answer: To compare them against the pots with fungus to see if the fungus was actually causing the change

questions.question: Based on the passage, what does the word 'conclusive' mean?
choices: Confusing and difficult to understand
Providing a clear and certain end to a doubt
Taking a very long time to complete
Happening by accident or luck
questions.answer: Providing a clear and certain end to a doubt

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Maya's hypothesis?
choices: Lilies are harder to grow than daisies
If fungus is present in the soil, then the lilies will wilt
All plants in the garden need more sunlight
Grandmothers always have the best gardens
questions.answer: If fungus is present in the soil, then the lilies will wilt
